'''Stephen Graham''' (born June 11, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player  coach. Graham's twin brother, [[Joey Graham|Joey]], was his college teammate and has also played in the NBA.

==High school and college career==
Born in [[Wilmington, Delaware]], Graham played competitively at [[Florida]]'s [[Brandon High School (Brandon, Florida)|Brandon High School]], and was team captain his senior year in which he averaged 16 points, 8 rebounds and 6 assists per game; in that year, he and his brother Joey led Brandon to the state finals. Graham was named to Hillsborough County's All-Conference team his junior year and to the All-State team his senior season. He played in the [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]]'s Junior Olympics National Game and was named an All-American. He was a member of both [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]]'s championship AAU Sunshine State Games' team, and Nike's traveling Florida team. He was recruited by South Florida, Richmond, Florida State and Florida.<ref name=okstate>{{cite web|url=http://www.okstate.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102504aaf.html|title=Stephen Graham|publisher=|access-date=2009-12-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606163013/http://www.okstate.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102504aaf.html|archive-date=2011-06-06|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Graham spent his freshman and sophomore [[college basketball]] seasons (2000–01; 2001–02) with the [[University of Central Florida]] [[UCF Knights men's basketball|Knights]], then transferred to Oklahoma State University for his junior year (2002–03) in which he redshirted.<ref name=okstate/> In his first season with the Cowboys in 2003–04, he only twice scored 12 points, his season-high.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=3425&year=2004|title=NCAA College Basketball Players – NCAA Basketball – ESPN|publisher=}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He averaged a mere 2.8 points, 1.4 rebounds and 0.7 assists per game overall,<ref name=espnstats>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/2832/stephen-graham|title=Stephen Graham|publisher=}}</ref> but he was named first-team Academic All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] for his academic achievements.<ref name=okstate/> A highlight in his senior season in 2004–05 was leading the Cowboys with 22 points in a 78–75 home loss to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] on December 28, 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=243630197|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041229165113/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=243630197|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 29, 2004|title=Gonzaga vs. Oklahoma State – Game Recap – December 28, 2004 – ESPN|publisher=}}</ref> For his second and final season for Oklahoma State, he averaged 6.5 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game.<ref name=espnstats/>

==Professional career==
After playing through his senior year with the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]], Graham declared for the [[2005 NBA draft]]. However, he was not selected. He played for the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the Las Vegas Summer League, and then for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] during the 2005 preseason, but was not offered a longer contract by either team. He then joined the [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]], a minor league, signing with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]. Graham was signed by the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Houston Rockets]] on December 10, 2005, but was cut on December 29 after playing in six games.<ref>{{cite web | title = Rockets Release Stephen Graham | url = http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/Rockets_release_Stephen_Graham-162604-822.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2005-12-29 | accessdate = 2009-10-24}}</ref>

After returning to the Skyforce in the interim, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]] on January 17, 2006.<ref>{{cite web |last=NBA |authorlink=National Basketball Association |title=Stephen Graham Info Page |website=[[NBA.com]] |publisher= |date= |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/stephen_graham |format= |doi= |accessdate=2007-10-12 }}</ref> He played his first game in a Bulls uniform three days later against the Rockets. However, Graham saw limited playing time with the Bulls and his contract was not extended when it expired.

On February 6, Graham was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Cavaliers Sign Stephen Graham to 10-Day Contract | url = http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/sign_graham_060206.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2006-02-06 | accessdate = 2009-10-24}}</ref> On February 20, he was signed to a second 10-day contract,<ref>{{cite web | title = Cavaliers Sign Stephen Graham to a Second 10-Day Contract | url = http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/sign_graham_060220.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2006-02-20 | accessdate = 2009-10-24}}</ref> then for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web | title = Cavaliers Sign Stephen Graham; Waive Nailon | url = http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/graham_nailon_060224.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2006-02-24 | accessdate = 2009-10-24}}</ref>

He spent the first two months of the [[2006–07 NBA season]] with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], but was waived on January 2, 2007, playing with an old acquaintance, the Skyforce in [[South Dakota]], who were now a part of the [[NBA G League|D-League]].

In July 2007, he signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.montgomerysportsgroup.com/swen/news_renew.php?subaction=showfull&id=1184681820&archive=&start_from=&ucat=4& |title=Stevie Signs with the Pacers |access-date=2007-11-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071224012553/http://www.montgomerysportsgroup.com/swen/news_renew.php?subaction=showfull&id=1184681820&archive=&start_from=&ucat=4& |archive-date=2007-12-24 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] in September 2009.<ref>[http://www.ktul.com/news/stories/0909/663702.html Five Former OSU Players On NBA Training Camp Rosters]{{Dead link|date=June 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=no }}</ref>

On September 15, 2010, Graham signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]].<ref>{{cite web | title = NETS Sign Free-Agent Forward Stephen Graham | url = http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Stephen_Graham_Release_100915.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2010-09-15 | accessdate = 2010-09-16}}</ref> The Nets waived Graham on December 22, 2011, following the [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Stephenson|first=Colin|title=Nets waive swingman Stephen Graham|url=http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2011/12/nets_waive_swingman_stephen_gr.html|work=The Star-Ledger|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120109194642/http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2011/12/nets_waive_swingman_stephen_gr.html|archive-date=January 9, 2012|date=December 22, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 13, 2012, Graham was acquired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Fort-Wayne-Mad-Ants/3/Transaction_History/2012 |title=Fort Wayne Mad Ants Transactions - RealGM |access-date=2015-04-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215134000/http://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Fort-Wayne-Mad-Ants/3/Transaction_History/2012 |archive-date=2014-12-15 }}</ref>

On September 30, 2013, Graham signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14372|title=Bucks add Junior Cadougan, Olek Czyz, Stephen Graham, Trey McKinney Jones to training camp :InsideHoops|date=30 September 2013 |publisher=}}</ref> However, he was waived on October 26.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14654|title=Milwaukee Bucks waive Trey McKinney Jones, Olek Czyz and Stephen Graham :InsideHoops|date=26 October 2013 |publisher=}}</ref>

On December 21, 2013, Graham signed with [[Guaros de Lara (basketball)|Guaros de Lara]].<ref>http://www.basketball.realgm.com/international/league/82/Venezuelan-LPB/team/1074/Guaros/transactions/2014{{Dead link|date=June 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=no }}</ref>

Graham competes for the Ants Alumni in [[The Basketball Tournament]]. He was a forward on the 2015 team who made it to the semifinals, falling 87–76 to [[Team 23]].

==Coaching career==
On October 21, 2015, he was hired by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] to work as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5061877|title=Mad Ants Finalize Coaching Staff for 2015–16 Season|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 21, 2015|accessdate=October 21, 2015}}</ref>

He was announced as a player development coach for the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-2016-17-coaches-091416|title = Meet the 2016–17 Nuggets Coaches| website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> On May 30, 2025, it was announced that Graham and the Nuggets would be parting ways.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nuggets defensive coordinator Ryan Saunders, other assistant coaches not retained under David Adelman|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/05/30/nuggets-coaching-staff-ryan-saunders-contract-not-renewed/|access-date=June 8, 2025|website=denverpost.com|language=en}}</ref>
